stories.title: Student protests in Tirana turn violent, targeting ministry buildings
stories.summary: Thousands of students marched in Tirana, beginning outside the Ministry of Education on Tuesday to demand better university conditions and job prospects. On the following day, part of the education ministry building was set on fire and the prime minister’s office, finance and interior ministries, as well as nearby businesses, were attacked. Protesters wearing gas masks and balaclavas threw rocks and firecrackers at the ministry gates.
stories.why: The violence marks a sharp escalation that could destabilize government operations and public order.
stories.change: New high-signal event entered the brief.

stories.title: IMF praises India's GDP methodology revamp, notes energy shock but strong fundamentals
stories.summary: The International Monetary Fund said it welcomed India’s recent overhaul of its gross domestic product (GDP) data collection and estimation methods. In the same comment, the IMF observed that India was facing an energy shock while its overall economic fundamentals remained robust.
stories.why: Changes in the global growth outlook can influence markets, trade, borrowing conditions and business investment across countries.
stories.previousTitle: IMF applauds India’s GDP data revamp, says country entered energy shock with strong fundamentals
stories.previousSummary: The International Monetary Fund praised India’s recent overhaul of its gross domestic product data and said the country has entered an energy shock while retaining strong economic fundamentals. This comment was reported in a headline by the Economic Times.

stories.title: US inflation exceeds forecasts for year to September
stories.summary: Official data show that US inflation rose more than forecasters expected for the 12‑month period ending in September. The increase was driven by higher petrol prices after disruptions to Middle‑East energy supplies linked to the US‑Israel conflict with Iran. The release comes in the final data set before the midterm elections, where cost‑of‑living issues dominate campaign discussion.
stories.why: Inflation data can shift expectations for central-bank interest rates, bond yields, borrowing costs and household purchasing power.
